fullDescription: A mobile photo editor app UI where the whole interface is a calibrated 18% grey card. The chrome is strictly achromatic: near-black top bar, histogram band and toolbar, white type, IBM Plex Mono readouts, and a neutral #737373 canvas the photograph sits on like a print on a grey mat, so the image is the only color on screen. The histogram is the photo's real luminance histogram, the clip warning and averages are measured from its pixels, and the preset thumbnails are the same photo under the exact CSS filters their labels print. Copy this design prompt for any photo editing app, camera tool, image workflow or media UI where the content should be the only color.
prompt:
## Resumo
A mobile PHOTO EDITOR screen built on one idea: the chrome is a calibrated 18% grey card. The canvas ground is neutral #737373 (relative luminance 0.17, the photographic grey-card standard, with a tiny mono '18% GREY' chip saying so), the top bar, histogram band and tool bar are near-black #0a0a0a, all type is white or near-white, and the photograph is the ONLY saturated element on screen, floating borderless on the grey mat like a print. Every number on screen is true of the displayed image: the histogram band draws the photo's actual 64-bucket luminance histogram as white bars with a small clip marker at the left toe, flanked by mono readouts (AVG 27%, SHADOWS CLIPPED 2.8%, HIGHLIGHTS 0.0%); the state is freshly imported with all six adjustment sliders parked at zero; the preset strip shows the same photo under real CSS filters, each labeled with its exact recipe; a muted EXIF row (24MM, F/4.0, 1/250, ISO 400) and an in-flow bottom tool bar (CROP, ADJUST active with a white underline, PRESETS, MASKS, INFO) close the screen. UI labels are Schibsted Grotesk tracked uppercase; every numeral and readout is IBM Plex Mono. Frameless, responsive, max-width 440px centered.

## Estilo Visual
Design a mobile photo editor screen as a calibrated darkroom instrument. Strictly achromatic chrome: a neutral #737373 grey-card canvas (R=G=B everywhere, zero blue or warm cast), near-black #0a0a0a bars and panels, white and near-white #fafafa type, hairline slider tracks in rgba(250,250,250,0.34). No gradients, no dot grids, no colored accents, no icon fonts; inline SVG icons only. The photograph is the ONLY saturated element on screen. UI labels in Schibsted Grotesk, small tracked uppercase; every numeral, parameter and readout in IBM Plex Mono. Include a tiny mono chip on the canvas mat reading 18% GREY. All on-screen data must be internally consistent with the displayed image and its zeroed edit state.

## Layout e Estrutura

### Top bar + grey-card canvas
A near-black #0a0a0a top bar: back chevron left, centered stack of the filename (11px tracked uppercase, e.g. IMG_4471.jpg) over a mono subline with the file's true dimensions and colorspace (800 x 533, sRGB), and a white EXPORT text button right. Below, the photograph sits borderless on the neutral #737373 grey-card mat with generous equal padding, a soft drop shadow, and a tiny mono chip top-left of the mat reading 18% GREY.

### Real histogram band
A full-width near-black #0a0a0a band containing the image's REAL luminance histogram: 64 white bars drawn as one SVG path in a 256x80 viewBox with preserveAspectRatio none stretched to full width, a thin white/20 baseline, and a small white triangle clip marker at the left toe. Beneath, three 10px IBM Plex Mono readouts spread across the band: AVG 27% left, a triangle icon plus SHADOWS CLIPPED 2.8% center in full white, HIGHLIGHTS 0.0% right. The histogram and readouts must be actual measured values of the displayed photo, never a decorative curve.

### Zeroed adjustment sliders
Six slider rows on the grey ground, one per adjustment (EXPOSURE, CONTRAST, HIGHLIGHTS, SHADOWS, WHITES, BLACKS): an 11px tracked uppercase label left, an IBM Plex Mono value right (0.00 for exposure stops, 0 for the rest), and a 1px rgba(250,250,250,0.34) hairline track with a 12px solid white round thumb parked exactly at center. The freshly-imported zero state is deliberate: the thumbs aligned at center-zero read as a calibrated instrument at rest.

### Live-filter preset strip + EXIF + tool bar
A horizontally scrolling strip of five 80px square thumbnails of the SAME photo, each with a real CSS filter applied and a 9px mono label printing its exact recipe: ORIGINAL none, MONO sat 0, FADE con .85 bri 1.1 sat .8, VELVIA sat 1.4 con 1.15, LIFT bri 1.15; let the fifth crop at the viewport edge as a scroll affordance. Below, a centered muted mono EXIF row: 24MM, F/4.0, 1/250, ISO 400, dot-separated. Close with a near-black tool bar: five buttons (CROP, ADJUST, PRESETS, MASKS, INFO), each a 20px inline-SVG stroke icon over a 9px tracked label, inactive at 50% opacity, active tool at full white with a white underline under its label.

## Componentes Especiais de UI

### Grey-card canvas mat — A neutral #737373 mat whose luminance is the photographic 18% grey standard, so the photo is judged against calibrated neutrality.
Make the editing canvas a flat neutral #737373 surface (strictly R=G=B, relative luminance about 0.17) with the photograph floating borderless on it under a soft shadow, generous equal margins on all sides, and a small IBM Plex Mono chip top-left reading 18% GREY in white on a translucent dark pill. No texture, no gradient; the mat's neutrality is the feature.

### True luminance histogram band — The photo's actual histogram drawn as data, with a clip marker and measured readouts, not a decorative waveform.
Compute the displayed image's 64-bucket luminance histogram and draw it as a single white SVG path (bars) in a 256x80 viewBox stretched full-width on a near-black band, with a hairline baseline, a small white triangle marker at the clipped left edge, and mono readouts for average luminance, shadow clip percentage and highlight clip percentage that match the image exactly.

### Recipe-labeled live preset chips — Preset thumbnails that are the same photo under the real CSS filter their label prints, so every chip proves itself.
Build a preset strip where each 80px thumbnail is the SAME source photo with an actual CSS filter applied inline (e.g. filter: saturate(0) for MONO, contrast(.85) brightness(1.1) saturate(.8) for FADE, saturate(1.4) contrast(1.15) for VELVIA, brightness(1.15) for LIFT) and a two-line 9px mono caption printing the preset name over its exact parameter recipe. The label and the transform must always agree.

### Center-zero hairline slider row — An adjustment row reading as an instrument at rest: hairline track, massy white thumb at dead center, mono value.
Compose a slider row with an 11px tracked uppercase label on the left, an IBM Plex Mono value on the right, and a full-width 1px track at rgba(250,250,250,0.34) carrying a 12px solid white circular thumb positioned exactly at 50% for the zero state. The track stays a hairline and the thumb carries the mass, never the reverse.

### In-flow achromatic tool bar — A five-tool bottom bar with inline-SVG stroke icons, tiny tracked labels, and a white underline marking the active tool.
End the screen with a near-black #0a0a0a tool bar of five evenly spread buttons: a 20px inline-SVG stroke icon (square linecaps, 1.5px stroke) above a 9px tracked uppercase label, for CROP, ADJUST, PRESETS, MASKS, INFO. Inactive tools sit at 50% opacity; the active tool is full white with a short white underline beneath its label. All icons strictly achromatic.

style.description: Darkroom instrument minimalism, strictly achromatic. A neutral mid-grey ground (#737373, the 18% grey card) carries near-black #0a0a0a panels, #fafafa/#ffffff type, and hairline tracks in low-alpha white; there are no gradients, no textures, no colored accents, and no decorative icons anywhere in the chrome. Color discipline is the whole point: the photograph being edited is the only chroma on screen, so the eye judges it truly, the way photographers judge exposure against a grey card. Data is always monospaced (IBM Plex Mono), labels are small tracked uppercase in a neutral grotesk (Schibsted Grotesk), and honesty is the aesthetic: the histogram, averages, clip warnings and preset labels all state measured facts of the visible image.
